place.en: Gangauri Bazaar · the noon dabba run · 12:40 PM

brief.en: Tiffin 114 left Gangauri Bazaar at four minutes past twelve and never reached Surajgarh Haveli. Sixty dabbas made the run. Fifty-nine arrived. When the carrier turned up at the Chandpole stand that evening it was empty except for a block of wax.

iraNote.en: “Both lines of that register are in one handwriting. Ask who was holding the pen.”

text.en: 114 · Surajgarh Haveli · signed out 12:04. Never signed in.

label.en: WAX BLOCK · IN THE EMPTY CARRIER

text.en: A key mold, pressed once. The cuts are clean and the edges are not — no lock-pick made this.
Tiffin 114 weighed 1.9 kg out. Every other dabba on the run: 1.2.
12:31 — one tiffin in. 12:33 — one tiffin out. Same hand, both lines.

label.en: CHIT · FOUND IN A DURWAN’S POCKET

text.en: “114. Don’t open it. Fifty rupees.” No signature.
Haveli gate → Chandpole, 12:40. One parcel, no passenger. Paid before the driver was told where.
One gold ear stud in on the 8th. Redeemed on the 12th, in cash.

label.en: LAB SLIP · CURD ON THE GATE STEP

dismissNote.en: ruled out — sixty dabbas cross that step at noon and every one of them leaks

text.en: Pigeons on the arch, and a shadow under them that isn’t a bird.

dismissNote.en: ruled out — a shadow on a wall is not a person

text.en: One cycle, stood from 12:10 to 1:40. Both hours paid.

dismissNote.en: ruled out — it says where a cycle was, not where a boy was

hook.en: carried 114 · the last man to hold it

alibi.en: He handed 114 over at the gate at 12:31 and the register says so — in somebody else’s handwriting.

hook.en: kept the gate · kept the register · kept the pen

confession.en: Fifty rupees to take one tiffin off the runner, put it in a rickshaw, and not look inside. He didn’t look. He could tell by the weight it wasn’t lunch, and he took the money anyway.

hook.en: packed 114 · works wax and dough daily

alibi.en: He packed 114 at ten to twelve in front of the whole kitchen. The wax was his. The fifty rupees were not.
He was paid before he was told where to go, which is a driver’s good luck and nobody’s crime.

hook.en: at the gate that morning · holds the durwan’s paper

alibi.en: He took an ear stud on the 8th and gave it back on the 12th. A man owed money does not steal a lunch to get it.

correction.en: A motive is fifty rupees folded in a pocket. Curd on a step is a Tuesday.
A shadow on an arch is not opportunity. One hand wrote that tiffin in and wrote it out again two minutes later.
Nothing walked out of that gate. It was driven — and the fare was settled before the driver knew the address.

text.en: “He never lets me sign. Not once, not in two years.”
“It came folded under the ledger on Tuesday. Fifty rupees and one line. I never saw a hand.”
“I packed what I was given. I did not look at it and I was not asked to.”

dismissNote.en: ruled out — a man saying he didn’t look is not evidence that he did

setting.en: The cycle stand at Gangauri, with his cap in his hands.

answer.en: “The durwan, sahib. At the gate, like always. He signs, I go.”

note.en: Like always. So the handover was normal — it is what happened after it that isn’t.

answer.en: “All of them are heavy in Teej week. I don’t weigh them, I carry them.”

note.en: He didn’t notice. A boy carrying sixty of them wouldn’t.

ask.en: The register says 114 went in at 12:31 and out at 12:33. Whose handwriting is that?

answer.en: “Girdhar sahib’s. Both lines. He never lets me sign — says my writing is bad.”

lockedHint.en: Pin the gate register first — you can’t put a page to a boy you haven’t read.

note.en: Both lines in one hand, and now the hand has a name on it.

setting.en: The gate. He answers standing, because he will not sit down for this.

ask.en: What is a block of wax doing in an empty tiffin?

answer.en: “I didn’t open it. I was told not to open it.”

note.en: Told not to. By whom is the next question, and he knows it.

ask.en: Fifty rupees, and a chit with no name on it. Who wrote it?

answer.en: “It came folded, under the gate ledger, on the Tuesday. I never saw a hand.”

lockedHint.en: The chit is still on the board. Pin it and he has something to answer.

note.en: He never saw who paid him. That is either the truth or the single most useful thing he could say.

answer.en: “Into a rickshaw. I don’t ask where rickshaws go.”

note.en: He put it in the rickshaw. That is the charge, and he has just said it out loud.

setting.en: The kitchen at four in the afternoon, between two meals.

ask.en: Why does a cook keep sealing wax?

answer.en: “For the pickle jars. Every kitchen in Rajasthan has a block of it.”

note.en: True, and unhelpful. Half the city could have cut that mold.

answer.en: “Heavier. I packed it heavier because I was told to. Extra for the guests.”

note.en: Told to, again. Everybody in this case was told something by somebody they cannot name.

ask.en: The scale says 1.9 against 1.2. What went in with the lunch?

answer.en: “I packed lunch. I don’t pack what I’m not given.”

lockedHint.en: Pin the weight slip — the difference is the only reason to ask.

note.en: He put in what he was handed. Somebody did the handing.

bankedClue.en: A wax key mold — cut by someone who’s never picked a lock

text.en: One man wrote the tiffin in and wrote it out again two minutes later. What was in his pocket while he did it?
